title: Tiered Eval Fidelity Contract and Shadow Mesh Playbook
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Summary
-------
This playbook defines a standardized, tiered fidelity contract for evaluation (Tiered Eval Fidelity Contract — TEFC) and prescribes the operational pattern we call the "Shadow Mesh" for validating model changes across Dedicated/Private/Hosted deployments. It provides concrete acceptance gates, telemetry requirements, and deterministic fallback behaviors for quantized and KV-cache-sensitive deployments.

Why this exists
----------------
- Reduce costly rollbacks by enforcing graded trust across fidelity bands (smoke -> nominal -> fidelity -> canary).
- Make quantized rollout decisions reproducible and auditable.
- Provide a lightweight mesh for cross-environment shadowing that preserves privacy budgets and cost constraints.

Scope
-----
Applies to: model promotions for text generation and chat endpoints (all sequence lengths), quantized artifacts (Q4/INT8/FP16), and any candidate that will be routed under Redwood’s smart routing policies. Not intended for multi-modal binary-only models (see separate multimodal playbook).

Terminology
-----------
- Fidelity Band: A named level of eval fidelity with SLOs and required checks.
- Shadow Mesh: cluster of shadow runners that mirror live traffic under controlled sampling and resource limits.
- Eval Contract: machine-readable manifest (YAML) defining probes, thresholds, and fallback policy for a promotion.

Fidelity Bands and Acceptance Criteria
-------------------------------------
Each model candidate must declare a TEFC manifest (example below). The platform enforces band-specific checks:

1) SMOKE (fast sanity)
   - Purpose: detect catastrophic regressions before longer runs.
   - Requirements: 500 synthetic probes (representative slices), >=99% pass on hard-blocking sentinels (safety & PII), latency p95 < 3x baseline.
   - Allowed deviations: None on safety sentinels.

2) NOMINAL (basic functional)
   - Purpose: baseline functional equivalence for common slices.
   - Requirements: 10k probes spread across top-20 slices, mean coherence delta <= 0.03 on primary metrics, token-cost delta <= +10%.
   - Allowed deviations: up to 2% of non-critical slices may regress if justified and triaged.

3) FIDELITY (quality-first)
   - Purpose: capture nuanced regressions across rare slices and long-context behavior.
   - Requirements: 100k probes including long-context multi-turn sequences, multi-seed aggregation with variance budgeting, embedding drift <= 0.02, function-call fidelity measured on heldout contract.
   - Allowed deviations: requires peer review and an annotated remediation plan for any failing slice.

4) CANARY (production shadow)
   - Purpose: final production verification with live traffic in Shadow Mesh.
   - Requirements: 24–72 hour Shadow Mesh run with sampled traffic (default 1% but configurable by tenant), SLOs: latency p95 <= 1.5x baseline, error-rate delta <= 0.1% absolute, quality SLA (Fidelity band metrics) met on 99% of critical slices.

TEFC Manifest (example)
-----------------------
YAML manifest attached to every model promotion. Required fields: model_id, baseline_model, fidelity_profile, probe_sets (ids), shadow_sampling, quant_profiles (if applicable), fallback_policy_id. Example: 

---
model_id: redwood-mosaic-v2-q8n
baseline_model: redwood-mosaic-v2-fp16
fidelity_profile: fidelity
probe_sets: [longcontext_multi_turn_v3, top20_slices_2026Q1]
shadow_sampling: 0.01
quant_profiles: [q8n-standard, q8n-latency-hedge]
fallback_policy_id: fallback-policy-quant-01
---

Shadow Mesh Architecture and Controls
------------------------------------
- Shadow runners are isolated containers that receive replicated requests (request shim) with sensitive payload redaction and synthetic identity mapping.
- Mesh supervisor (service: eval-mesh-orchestrator) coordinates rollout phasing, telemetry collection, and automatic escalation.
- Resource limits: default mesh pool per model = 10% of baseline capacity, capped at absolute 100 vCPU-equivalents and 32GB GPU VRAM. These limits are enforced to avoid production interference.
- Privacy gating: PII-sensitive requests are dropped from the mesh by the PII-filter service using deterministic rules (see PII-filter spec link).

Telemetry and Required Signals
------------------------------
All TEFC runs must emit the following signal set to the telemetry pipeline:
- probe_id, slice_id, seed_id (for multi-seed runs)
- latency_ms (p50,p95,p99)
- token_count_in/out, token_cost_estimate
- top-k logits entropy and mean confidence
- embedding_cosine_to_baseline (for embedding stability)
- sentinel_safety_violations (boolean + violation_class)
- kv_cache_hit_rate (per-request)
- quant_fallback_triggered (boolean)

For canaries: distributed tracing (trace_id) and request sampling traces must be produced at 100% for flagged errors and 0.1% otherwise.

Onboarding Checklist (Model Owners)
----------------------------------
1) Create TEFC manifest and attach probe_sets.
2) Run SMOKE locally and upload results to eval-store.
3) Schedule NOMINAL run via eval-orchestrator (estimated cost and runtime shown in UI).
4) If NOMINAL passes, run FIDELITY; tag all failing slices and assign mitigations.
5) Request CANARY start and configure shadow_sampling.
6) Monitor mesh dashboard and run final acceptance sign-off via the model promotion UI.

Operational Play: Rollout and Rollback
-------------------------------------
1) Promotion begins in SMOKE. If any hard sentinel fails, immediate stop and block with auto-notification to owner.
2) NOMINAL/FIDELITY runs produce a triage report (auto-generated): top regressions, suggested fixes (quant profile swap, prompt rewrite, increased KV cache bucket).
3) CANARY begins: mesh supervisor incrementally ramps sampling from 0.1% to configured sampling over 6 hours while verifying telemetry gates every 30 minutes.
4) Automatic rollback triggers (immediate circuit-break): any safety sentinel violation, latency p95 > 2x baseline for 3 consecutive windows, or quant_fallback_triggered rate > 5% in a 15-min window.
5) Manual rollback: owner or SRE can trigger immediate rollback via the Console with justification. The rollback record is stored in audit logs (policy: retain 1 year).

Quantization Handoff and Fallback Patterns
-----------------------------------------
- Quant profiles must be enumerated in the TEFC manifest with explicit hedges: (e.g., q8n-latency-hedge -> fallback q4n-stability).
- Fallback behaviors: runtime will attempt up to N retries (default 2) with progressively higher-fidelity variants before falling back to baseline FP16.
- Quant-quality delta budgets are enforced: e.g., coherence_delta_budget <= 0.04 per-slice. Exceeding budget requires approval from Applied ML.

Regression Triage Workflow
-------------------------
- When a failed slice is detected, the triage ticket is auto-created with: slice_id, example inputs, baseline and candidate responses, token-delta, and recommended remediation.
- Triage levels: L0 (auto), L1 (owner-only), L2 (cross-team review), L3 (exec escalation).
- Time-to-first-action targets: L0 = 15m, L1 = 4h, L2 = 24h.
- For quant-related regressions, attach quant-profile artifacts and run the quant-replay harness (CLI example below).

CLI: running a local TEFC smoke test
------------------------------------
# assumes redwood-cli installed and AUTH_TOKEN set
redwood-cli eval run --manifest ./tefc.yaml --mode smoke --upload-results 

# replay a failure slice in quant harness
redwood-cli quant replay --artifact s3://quant-artifacts/q8n-latency-hedge.tar.gz --slice-id slice_98765 --seeds 5 --out results/

Metrics Dashboard (required widgets)
-----------------------------------
- Band-pass heatmap: per-slice pass/fail for each fidelity band (SMOKE/NOMINAL/FIDELITY/CANARY).
- Token-economy delta: cost and token count deltas against baseline.
- Safety sentinel trend: violations per 1k requests.
- Quant-fallback events: rate and correlated latencies.
- KV cache occupancy and hit-rate by tenant.

Ownership and Escalation
------------------------
- Model owner: primary responsible for manifest, probe selection, and remediation.
- Applied ML team: enforcement of fidelity contracts and review of FIDELITY-level regressions.
- SRE: Shadow Mesh operation, resource limits, and automated rollbacks.
- Security/Privacy: PII-filter rule updates and approvals for shadowing policies.

Appendix: Example triage report (snippet)
----------------------------------------
| field | value |
|---|---:|
| slice_id | rare-nested-references-41 |
| baseline_resp_coherence | 0.86 |
| candidate_resp_coherence | 0.71 |
| token_delta | +18% |
| kv_cache_hit_rate | 42% |
| suggested_action | switch quant profile to q8n-stability; add 2 exemplars to longcontext probe; re-run FIDELITY |

Notes and caveats
------------------
- TEFC is intentionally prescriptive for higher-risk models; lightweight services may opt into a relaxed contract with approval.
- Cost: FIDELITY band runs are expensive — budget owners must approve before scheduling (UI enforces billing gates).
